title: Busko's work rules out plate defects in the transients

tellings.quote:
so apparently that proves that these
These patterns aren't from chemical
stains or plate defects, but from the
light actually hit the optical circuitry
of the telescope itself.

plain: Strange brief points of light on photographic sky plates from the late 1950s, which the astronomer Beatriz Villarroel calls transients, were not caused by chemical stains or flaws in the plates but by real light passing through the telescope's optics, according to work by the astronomer Ivo Busko. Michels relays this second-hand, saying it 'apparently' proves the point. If so, it would mean something real was shining in the sky when those plates were taken.
